subject: proj-dy
title: (R)PROJ.DY.------GRAD.
description: Diagram in MP(II)-19, the section on Africa as the site of the next political transformation. The prose above the diagram identifies its argument: 'the dynamics of the next transition in Africa will be very interesting for what its liberation will means to alternative functionalism. Because the seriousness of colonial manipulation has created a necessarily complex situation for information dynamics and expansion dictates.' The crossing diagrams that complexity: (R)PROJ-DY (the reality of projectional dynamics) is crossed with GRAD (gradualism — the temporal pacing the colonial situation has made structurally necessary). PROJ-DY sits at the lower-left with the subject-arrow; TRS (transition) rises from the main line, ALT-F (alternative functionalism) branches from the TRS line to the top-left, and T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) branches from the ALT-F line to the left margin. GRAD sits at upper center-right as partner-axis, at the end of the main line. CULT-AF-B (culture affinity basis) branches from the main line down to the right; MT-INFO (multi-information) branches from the CULT-AF-B line to the right margin, with INT (intention) branching from the MT-INFO line. POL-DY (political dynamics) drops from the CULT-AF-B line to the bottom-center; INFO-COMP (information compression) branches from the POL-DY line, and INTR (interpretation) from the INFO-COMP line. Structural argument: when projectional-dynamics is crossed with gradualism, the diagonal from TRS up to ALT-F shows the subject's path through transition into alternative-functionalism — but ALT-F has *no edge* back to GRAD on the partner-axis.
